inspiration: Armour as texture layers: one body texture per character, with equipment textures composited onto body regions (arms, torso, legs, hands, feet) by item type. Our version could use our own body paint and armour layers, with a region map per armour class.

Armour as mesh toggles: equipment shows or hides mesh sections (wristbands, trousers and so on) instead of adding separate meshes, so cloth and plate fit without clipping. Our version could toggle body sections per armour piece.

Water that fades at the shore: transparency depends on depth (shallow clear, deep dark blue), with a shore blend driven by a depth map. Recreate with a painted or computed depth mask and our own water hue.

Fog that matches the horizon: fog colour is set equal to the horizon colour so distance fades into the sky. Sun and moon discs are placed from the time of day. Our version could use per-biome colour sets.
Character composite: base skin, face and underwear are baked into one texture, and hair is laid onto the scalp region so it works under a helm. Our version could bake our own layers the same way.
UI from layout files: an XML-style layout parser builds a frame tree, with Lua hooks for behaviour. Our HUD could be described the same way (layout file plus scripts), with our own widget set.

briefs.label: Layered plate chest
briefs.why: Armour reads as a real overlay on the body, so changing gear costs one texture rebuild.
briefs.keep: A region map per armour class; overlay textures composited onto a shared body; mesh sections toggled per piece.
briefs.change: Our own region set (for example separate pauldrons); a different silhouette through section toggles; our own trim motif.

briefs.label: Shore-fade lake
briefs.why: A depth-based fade makes water read as a body of water, not a flat sheet.
briefs.keep: Clear shallows and dark deep water; a shore fade driven by depth; an edge highlight.
briefs.change: Our own water hue and foam pattern; a different shallows colour per biome; wave pattern per zone.

briefs.label: Horizon-matched dusk
briefs.why: Fog that matches the horizon hides the seam between the world and the sky.
briefs.keep: Fog colour equal to the horizon colour; a sun disc placed by time of day; gradient bands.
briefs.change: A colour set per biome; a different moon and star layout; our own cloud shapes.
